mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about algae reflects a common misconception?

options.B: Algae are photosynthetic and contain chlorophyll a.
options.C: Algae can be unicellular, filamentous or multicellular.
options.D: Algae possess diverse pigments such as chlorophylls, carotenoids and phycobilins.

mcqs.explanation: Many students think algae live only in the sea, but algae occur in both marine and freshwater habitats. Options B, C and D correctly describe general features of algae, whereas option A is a misconception.

mcqs.question: A newly discovered aquatic photosynthetic organism contains chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, carotenoids, stores starch inside its cells, and has a filamentous thallus. To which major algal group does it most likely belong?
mcqs.explanation: Green algae (Chlorophyceae) possess chlorophyll a and b, carotenoids, store starch within the chloroplast, and often have filamentous thalli. Brown algae have chlorophyll c and fucoxanthin, red algae have phycobilins, and diatoms are unicellular with silica frustules. Hence option A is the correct classification.

mcqs.question: Which characteristic most clearly distinguishes members of the Chlorophyceae from members of the Phaeophyceae and Rhodophyceae?

options.A: Presence of chlorophyll b as an accessory pigment
options.B: Storage of starch within the chloroplast
options.C: Cell walls composed mainly of cellulose
options.D: Pigments include phycobilins as the dominant accessory pigment

mcqs.answer: Presence of chlorophyll b as an accessory pigment
mcqs.explanation: Chlorophyceae (green algae) contain chlorophyll b in addition to chlorophyll a, giving them a green colour. Brown algae (Phaeophyceae) have chlorophyll c and fucoxanthin, while red algae (Rhodophyceae) contain phycobilins as dominant pigments. Options B and C are not exclusive to Chlorophyceae, and option D describes red algae, not green algae.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the Phaeophyceae (brown algae)?

options.A: Dominant accessory pigment fucoxanthin giving a brown colour
options.B: Storage of glycogen as the primary food reserve
options.D: Production of flagellated zoospores as the only reproductive unit

mcqs.answer: Dominant accessory pigment fucoxanthin giving a brown colour
mcqs.explanation: Brown algae contain chlorophyll a, chlorophyll c and the brown-coloured accessory pigment fucoxanthin, which masks other pigments and gives them their characteristic colour. They store laminarin (a polysaccharide), not glycogen, have cell walls of cellulose and alginates (not chitin), and reproduce via various spores and gametophytes, not solely flagellated zoospores. Hence option A is correct.
